description: Age gates, pre-exercise screening and safe calorie and weight-change limits. Entries with "origin": "source" carry a sourceId and reproduce a published figure. Entries with "origin": "app_policy" are conservative guards chosen for this app; they are not attributed to any publication and are labelled as app rules in the UI.

disclaimer.text: This app gives general fitness and nutrition information based on WHO and ICMR-NIN guidelines. It is not medical advice and does not replace a doctor or dietitian. Consult a qualified doctor before starting any exercise or diet program, especially if you have a health condition, are pregnant, are under 18 or over 60. Stop immediately and seek medical help if you feel chest pain, dizziness, severe breathlessness or sharp pain.

ageRules.message: This app is not built for children under 13. Please use it together with a parent and a doctor, who can plan activity and food that is right for this age.
Under 18 you get activity guidance only. This app will not set a calorie deficit or a weight-loss target for you. Growth and nutrition at this age should be planned with a doctor or dietitian.

Because you are 60 or older, this app starts you on a lighter default intensity and adds balance and strength work. Please talk to your doctor before you start, and stop any exercise that causes pain, dizziness or breathlessness.
ageRules.supportingNote: ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024 treats over 60 years as the elderly band and recommends additional strength and functional balance activity on three or more days a week. It also advises that men and women over 40 consult a doctor before starting a vigorous activity programme. WHO 2020 uses 65 years and older for its older adult recommendations.

weightReductionFloorKcal.note: Weight reduction diets should not be less than 1000 kcal/day and should provide all nutrients.

maxDeficitPercentOfNeeds.note: It is advisable not to go beyond a 40% energy deficit of daily energy needs, so that muscle mass and protein balance are maintained.

typicalDeficitRangeKcal.note: A typical energy-deficient weight loss diet is a 500-750 kcal/day deficit.

bmrFloor.note: This app never sets a daily calorie target below the user's own resting energy expenditure calculated with the Mifflin-St Jeor equation. The equation is published; using it as a lower bound is this app's safety choice.

defaultLoseDeficitKcal.note: Default starting deficit for a Lose goal, kept inside the published 500-750 kcal range and then clamped by the floor and maximum-deficit rules.

defaultGainSurplusKcal.note: Default starting surplus for a Gain goal.

stallAdjustmentKcal.note: If measured weight has not moved towards the goal across two consecutive weekly check-ins, the daily target is adjusted by this amount and then re-clamped by all safe limits.

maxLossKgPerWeek.note: A reduction of half a kilogram of body weight per week is considered to be safe. Rapid weight loss approaches should be avoided.

maxLossPercentBodyWeightPerWeek.note: Additional guard so that the weekly loss cap never exceeds 1% of current body weight. This matters for lighter users, for whom half a kilogram would be a larger share of body weight.

minBmiForWeightLossGoal.note: The Lose goal is disabled below a BMI of 18.5, which ICMR-NIN gives as the lower end of the normal BMI range for Indian adults.

maxGainKgPerWeek.note: Weekly cap for a Gain goal, set to the same half a kilogram per week that ICMR-NIN gives as a safe rate of change, so that a surplus cannot run away. The default Gain surplus of 300 kcal/day sits inside this cap.

questionnaire.note: Pre-exercise screening questions written for this app, in the style of a readiness questionnaire. They are a safety prompt only. This app does not diagnose anything and does not replace a medical assessment. ICMR-NIN advises that people with chronic disease, and anyone over 40 starting vigorous activity, consult a doctor first.

dailyCheck.note: Asked every single time the user taps Start Workout.

weeklyCheck.note: Asked at every weekly check-in. A yes answer pauses automatic diet changes until the user clears it.
